meta.purpose: Advanced Examination Intelligence — chapter heatmaps, marks distribution, repeated-concept analysis, weakness diagnosis and mock recommendations across every CMA paper.

integrity.headline: Confirmed information and predictions are kept in separate sections and never mixed.
integrity.confirmed: Only the exam calendar and published section weights, each with a source and a verification date.
integrity.derived: Chapter-level marks are derived arithmetically from published section weights and are labelled indicative.
integrity.prediction: Themes and likely emphasis are professional estimates, clearly labelled, never presented as known fact.
integrity.copyright: ICMAI question papers and suggested answers are the Institute's intellectual property. This repository does not reproduce them. Record questions in your own words for personal study, or cite the source and page you are studying from.

examCalendar.status: confirmed — verify against the official ICMAI timetable before relying on any date

intermediateSchedule.paper: Financial Management and Business Data Analytics

notes: Group I papers fall on 10, 12, 14 and 16 December 2026; Group II papers on 11, 13, 15 and 17 December.
Results are normally declared within about eight weeks; do not plan anything that depends on the result date.
Admit card, centre and reporting time come from the ICMAI admit card, not from this file.

paperBlueprints.structureNote: Confirm the question pattern for your session from the ICMAI model question papers before your first mock.
paperBlueprints.writingTime: Allow 15 minutes for planning and 8–9 minutes per 5-mark question.
paperBlueprints.strategy: Companies Act first (40%), then contracts. Industrial law revised in the final three weeks.

paperBlueprints.structureNote: Practical paper — working notes carry the marks.
paperBlueprints.writingTime: Budget 20 minutes per 10-mark problem, and leave 10 minutes to check balancing.
paperBlueprints.strategy: Accounting Standards and final accounts first. Partnership practised to full-solution fluency.

paperBlueprints.structureNote: Verify which statute and which Finance Act amendments are examinable for your session — see the amendment watch in the tax knowledge base.
paperBlueprints.writingTime: Computation questions first; theory answers should be section-referenced and short.
paperBlueprints.strategy: GST (35%) and PGBP computations are the two biggest returns on effort.

paperBlueprints.structureNote: Predominantly practical; theory is a small but reliable block.
paperBlueprints.writingTime: 22–25 minutes per 10-mark problem, with a separate working-notes column.
paperBlueprints.strategy: Elements of cost, methods of costing and techniques are the three anchors. Target 25+ full problems a week.

paperBlueprints.structureNote: Mixed theory and numerical; OR questions reward procedure.
paperBlueprints.writingTime: Numericals first, then structured theory answers.
paperBlueprints.strategy: OR/PPC (20%) and project management (15%) are numerical and predictable.

paperBlueprints.writingTime: Accounting problems first while attention is highest.
paperBlueprints.strategy: Schedule III, cash flow and audit provisions carry the paper.

paperBlueprints.writingTime: Ratio, capital budgeting and working capital first.
paperBlueprints.strategy: Master the four core numerical blocks before touching analytics theory.

paperBlueprints.structureNote: Decision-oriented; presentation of the decision table matters.
paperBlueprints.writingTime: Marginal costing and decision questions first.
paperBlueprints.strategy: Marginal costing plus its applications is 30% — the single largest block in the course.

analyticsSpec.chapterHeatmap: Computed from two separate sources: (1) indicative marks per chapter derived from published section weights, and (2) your own logged attempts. The two are never combined into a single misleading score.
analyticsSpec.questionFrequency: Derived from your question log, not from an invented claim about past papers.
analyticsSpec.weaknessAnalysis: A chapter is weak when your logged accuracy is below 60% and your attempts are at least 3. Fewer than 3 attempts is 'insufficient evidence', not 'strong'.
analyticsSpec.revisionPriority: Priority = indicative marks × (1 − your accuracy) × recency of failure. Chapters with no attempts are flagged as unknown rather than assumed.
analyticsSpec.mockRecommendation: Recommends the next mock type based on attempts, accuracy and time since the last full-length paper.
